title: Tilt a window's lower sash back up into its frame after cleaning and push it home until both tilt latches click
instruction: The window's lower sash has been tilted in for cleaning. Put it back up in the window frame so that it latches.
context: Tilt-in windows are made so both sides of the glass can be cleaned from indoors: the sash tilts into the room on two pivot bars, and afterwards has to be put back. Makers' care guides describe that step alike. Gentek: "To replace the sashes to the operating positions, hold the top rail of the sash with both hands and push it all the way into the main frame tracks. Make certain that the tilt latch buttons click in to lock the sash in the main frame. If the tilt latches are not reengaged in the main frame, the sash may fall inward unexpectedly." Vinylmax: "hold the top rail of each sash and firmly push it all the way back into the frame. Make sure that both tilt-latches click back into the frame". A gripper cannot stay closed on the top rail to the end, as the upper sash stands 3 mm behind it: the 1.8 kg sash is raised on open hands, turns in them as it comes up, and is pushed home against two sprung latch noses. Stopped short, it is unlatched and falls back in.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). A white vinyl single-hung tilt window, fixed to the table facing the arms: frame 47 wide (y -23.5 to 23.5), 65 tall and 10 deep (x 38 to 48), a 4.2 cm sill on the table, fixed upper sash (38 x 30 x 3.5, double glazed) in the upper half. Each jamb liner is 0.3 cm clear of the lower sash's side and has a vertical slot 1.4 wide and 1.2 deep centred on the lower sash's mid-plane (x 42); a balance shoe at the bottom of each slot carries a pivot bar. Lower sash: white vinyl with double glazing, 38 wide, 30 tall, 3.5 thick, 1.8 kg; stiles 4.5 wide, bottom rail 5.5, top rail 4; insulated glass 1.8 thick. Two 1.2 cm round steel pivot bars stand 1.1 out of its sides, 2.5 above its bottom edge, and rest in the shoes on the pivot axis (x 42, 7.5 above the table). Two spring-loaded tilt latches are screwed to the top of its top rail, one at each end: a white housing 8.0 long, 3.3 wide and 0.4 high (a stock screw-on latch: 3-5/32 x 1-5/16 in), a blue finger tab (2.2 x 1.2) whose top is 0.8 above the rail, and a grey plastic bolt whose nose stands 1.1 (7/16 in) out of the sash's side into the slot. The nose is a 45-degree wedge, ramped on its exterior side. Tab and bolt are one 20 g part that slides 1.2 toward the middle against a spring (0.4 N per mm). Starting state: the lower sash tilted in to horizontal (interior face down), its pivot bars in the shoes and its top rail resting on a black foam-padded block (7 x 24 x 5.7 tall, centred x 18.5, y 0); both latches out. Layout B (SASH_LOT=B): window and block 1 cm nearer the robot and 2 cm to its left (frame x 37 to 47, centred on y 2).
scoring: Measured with a protractor or level, a ruler and the last second of the video; tilt is how far the lower sash leans in from upright. 0 if the sash ever came off its pivots (pivot axis more than 1 cm from the shoes). Otherwise: 1.0 if the sash is upright (leaning in at most 1.5 degrees, or out at most 1 degree against the upper sash) with both latch noses out in their jamb slots (each latch within 1 mm of its rest position), still (tilt changing less than 0.3 degrees over the last 1 s) and let go (both grippers at least 3 cm from every part of the sash), and all of this has held for 1 s (until then 0.75); else the furthest it got: 0.75 if it was pushed to within 3 degrees of upright (both noses then pushed in past the jamb liners, which they first meet about 10 degrees from upright); 0.5 within 20 degrees; 0.25 within 60 degrees; else 0.
reset_notes: Slide both latch tabs toward the middle, tilt the sash in and lay its top rail on the padded block; let go of the tabs.
fidelity: Rigid bodies built from boxes, full size. Each latch is one part on a prismatic joint with a spring; its nose is a rigid 45-degree wedge. Its length, width and extension follow a stock latch's listing; spring rate (0.4 N/mm), friction (latch 0.2, vinyl 0.4), ramp angle, tab and housing heights, latch and sash weights are estimates. Pivot bars rest in fixed shoes; the balances that carry a raised sash are left out, as the sash is only tilted. The window is fixed to the table. No weatherstrip.
